Adjacent Microsoft docs later clarified the generic `PowerRequestExecutionRequired` contract and the way audio playback keeps the audio stack active during connected-standby playback, but no current Microsoft page has been found that names this exact audio-specific internal setting. Later KVM local-KD passes first surfaced the exact symbol `nt!PopPowerRequestActiveAudioEnablesExecutionRequired` and then resolved its live current-build value as `1`, aligning the running kernel with the repo-doc default. A later static INIT-table follow-up then showed a current-build `ntoskrnl.exe` descriptor entry under `Power` that binds `AllowAudioToEnableExecutionRequiredPowerRequests` to the exact global later resolved by local KD as `nt!PopPowerRequestActiveAudioEnablesExecutionRequired`. Later follow-ups then showed `nt!PopUmpoSendPowerRequestOverrideQuery` packaging requester state for `nt!PopUmpoSendPowerMessage`, `nt!PopPowerRequestExecutionRequiredSettingCallback` staying timeout-setting specific by updating `nt!PopExecutionRequiredTimeout`, the timeout timer/worker chain feeding back into `nt!PopPowerRequestHandleExecutionEnablementUpdate`, the broader override-response plus callback-worker path staying queue and PDC driven with no visible `*PowerRequest*Reg*` symbol, and a generic power-setting callback subsystem around `PoRegisterPowerSettingCallback` and `PopInitializePowerSettingCallbacks`. A later host-side objdump follow-up then showed an unlabeled current-build `INIT` walker at `0x140C48AB8` uniquely consuming the broader `Power` descriptor table, passing row key and value names through subkey and value-lookup helpers before copying payload into the paired target global. A later Wave 4 ETW stackwalk plus grouped Ghidra follow-up then captured an exact current-build runtime query lane from `reg.exe` through `QueryValue`, `QueryRegistry`, `RegGetValueW`, `RegQueryValueExW`, `BaseRegQueryValueInternal`, `NtQueryValueKey`, and kernel-side `EtwpTraceRegistry`, `EtwpTraceStackWalk`, `KiSystemServiceStart`, and `ntoskrnl.exe!NtQueryValueKey`. The lane is strong enough for a schema-backed draft, but it still lacks a primary current-build doc for this exact audio-specific policy and the earlier boot/init seeding path remains open.

setting.name: Allow Audio To Enable Execution Required Power Requests
setting.casual_explanation: This appears to be a kernel-adjacent Control Power setting tied to whether active audio can enable execution-required power requests. It is being tracked as a research candidate, not a user-facing tweak.
setting.why_people_change_it: Kernel and power researchers may inspect this value when investigating how active audio sessions influence execution-required power-request behavior under undocumented power-policy flows.
setting.tradeoffs_overview: The value now has a stronger evidence chain because it has repo docs, observed baseline state, an exact current-build string hit, a retained enrichment recommendation, a repo-native trigger harness, adjacent Microsoft documentation for generic execution-required and audio-active behavior, a live KVM local-KD value that matches the repo-doc default, direct current-build consumer disassembly, a visible UMPO override-query lineage, a timeout-setting callback disassembly, a retained timeout timer/worker chain, a retained override-response plus callback-worker follow-up that still exposed no visible `*PowerRequest*Reg*` symbol, a retained generic power-setting callback infrastructure pass around `PoRegisterPowerSettingCallback`, a later host-side static walker analysis that materially closes the old seeding-path gap, and a later Wave 4 ETW stackwalk plus grouped Ghidra lane that proves an exact current-build runtime query path. It is still too weak for a published tweak because the seeding path is only statically inferred from current-build disassembly and Microsoft still does not publish the exact audio-specific internal setting.
setting.professional_notes: Repo power docs assign `AllowAudioToEnableExecutionRequiredPowerRequests = 1` under `Control\\Power` and map it to `PopPowerRequestActiveAudioEnablesExecutionRequired`. The power routing note later kept the value inside the `Control\\Power` docs cluster. The observed clean baseline then confirmed that the parent `Control\\Power` path exists while the value itself is absent. A later targeted current-build string batch found an exact Unicode hit for `AllowAudioToEnableExecutionRequiredPowerRequests` in `ntoskrnl.exe`, which is stronger than a pure docs-only mention and enough to keep the value out of raw backlog. Source-enrichment later retained the candidate in the canonical queue with `power-request-simulation` as the suggested trigger family, specifically `PowerCreateRequest(SystemRequired)`, `PowerSetRequest(DisplayRequired)`, and an audio playback session. A later repo-native follow-up then exposed that same trigger family as a named guest Procmon profile plus a matching mega-trigger runtime alias, closing the old trigger-design gap before the first dedicated narrow replay. Microsoft later documented the generic `PowerRequestExecutionRequired` contract and separately documented that connected-standby audio playback or auditory notification keeps the audio stack active while audio is being generated, which is useful adjacent context for this lane even though no current Microsoft page has been found that names `AllowAudioToEnableExecutionRequiredPowerRequests` itself. Later KVM local-KD passes first surfaced the exact symbol `nt!PopPowerRequestActiveAudioEnablesExecutionRequired` and then read its live current-build value as `1`, which matches the repo-doc default and keeps the lane out of pure docs-first territory. A later static INIT-table follow-up then found the exact current-build value-name string in `ntoskrnl.exe`, placed it inside an `INIT` descriptor slice under the shared `Power` key string, and matched the paired target-global pointer to `nt!PopPowerRequestActiveAudioEnablesExecutionRequired` via the retained local-KD symbol address. A later current-build disassembly pass then showed `nt!PopPowerRequestEvaluateExecutionRequiredStatus` directly comparing `nt!PopPowerRequestActiveAudioEnablesExecutionRequired` against the caller-supplied execution-required state, while `nt!PopPowerRequestExecutionRequiredSettingCallback` chained into the same reader family through `PopPowerRequestHandleExecutionmentUpdate`. A later wildcard lineage pass then showed that the current build exposes only one `*PowerRequest*Setting*` symbol, `nt!PopPowerRequestExecutionRequiredSettingCallback`, alongside `PopPowerRequestInitialize`, `PopPowerRequestOverrideInitialize`, and the `PopExecutionRequiredTimeout` family. A later init/override disassembly pass then showed `PopPowerRequestInitialize` only zeroing per-object fields and `PopPowerRequestOverrideInitialize` iterating `PopPowerRequestObjectList` before calling `PopUmpoSendPowerRequestOverrideQuery`, which is useful because it still did not expose a registry read in the visible current-build init path. A later dedicated UMPO disassembly pass then showed `PopUmpoSendPowerRequestOverrideQuery` storing requester identity via `PoStoreRequester`, allocating an `Umpo`-tagged buffer, and dispatching `PopUmpoSendPowerMessage`, while wildcard output exposed `PopUmpoSendPowerRequestCreate`, `PopUmpoSendPowerRequestAction`, and `PopUmpoSendPowerRequestOverrideCleanup`. A later dedicated callback disassembly pass then showed `PopPowerRequestExecutionRequiredSettingCallback` comparing the incoming GUID against `GUID_EXECUTION_REQUIRED_REQUEST_TIMEOUT`, requiring a 4-byte payload, writing `PopExecutionRequiredTimeout`, rearming `PopPowerRequestExecutionRequiredTimeoutTimer`, and then calling `PopPowerRequestHandleExecutionEnablementUpdate`. A later timeout-lineage pass then showed `PopPowerRequestSetExecutionRequiredTimeoutTimer` reading `PopExecutionRequiredTimeout`, comparing it against `PopExecutionRequiredContext`, and arming `PopPowerRequestExecutionRequiredTimeoutTimer` via `KeSetTimer2`, while `PopPowerRequestExecutionRequiredTimeoutCallback` simply queued work and `PopPowerRequestExecutionRequiredTimeoutWorker` re-entered `PopPowerRequestHandleExecutionEnablementUpdate`. A later response-lineage follow-up then showed `x nt!*PowerRequest*Reg*` returning no visible current-build symbols, `PopPowerRequestHandleRequestOverrideQueryResponse` updating request state, re-evaluating pending request status, and queueing `PopPowerRequestUpdateWorkItem`, `PopPowerRequestCallbackWorker` draining the update queue through `PopPowerRequestStatsSetActive` and `PopPowerRequestHandleRequestUpdate`, and `PopPowerRequestCallbackExecutionRequired` consulting `PoPdcCallbacks`, `PopPowerRequestPdcNotifiedExecutionRequired`, `PopPowerRequestPdcNotifiedSystemRequired`, `PopPowerRequestConvertSystemToExecution`, and `PopSIdle`. A later power-setting lineage pass then exposed the broader current-build infrastructure around this family: `x nt!*PowerSetting*` returned `PopInitializePowerSettingCallbacks`, `PopInitializePowerSettings`, `PoRegisterPowerSettingCallback`, `PoUnregisterPowerSettingCallback`, `PopDispatchPowerSettingCallbacks`, `PopCallPowerSettingCallback`, `PopQueryPowerSettingUlong`, `PopSetPowerSettingValue`, and `PopRegisteredPowerSettingCallbacks`, while `x nt!*ExecutionRequired*Setting*` still returned only `PopPowerRequestExecutionRequiredSettingCallback`. The same pass showed `PoRegisterPowerSettingCallback` allocating a callback object, copying the target GUID and callback pointer, and resolving the setting through `PopFindPowerSettingConfiguration`, which is strong proof that the visible execution-required family now sits on a generic power-setting callback subsystem even though the exact binding site for `PopPowerRequestExecutionRequiredSettingCallback` is still open. This matters because the visible family is now callback/init/timeout-setting/timer-worker/UMPO/override-response/PDC/power-setting-subsystem driven and still does not demonstrate a registry read or a direct write to `PopPowerRequestActiveAudioEnablesExecutionRequired`. A later host-side objdump/xref follow-up then narrowed the old seeding gap substantially: an unlabeled `INIT` walker at `0x140C48AB8` uniquely loads the broader `0x140C72E30` `Power` descriptor table, passes each row key string through `0x1407E334C`, each row value name through `0x14086A794` and `0x14086C510`, and the row target pointer through `0x140C4CB20`; this is best read as the current-build static registry seeding path for the execution-required pair even though the routine is not yet symbol-resolved and Microsoft still does not publish the exact audio-specific internal seed. A 2026-04-14 Wave 4 ETW stackwalk plus grouped Ghidra follow-up then captured an explicit `reg.exe query HKLM\\SYSTEM\\CurrentControlSet\\Control\\Power /v AllowAudioToEnableExecutionRequiredPowerRequests` lane, recorded exact `KeyName` hits in the ETW bundle, and resolved the caller stack into `reg.exe!QueryValue`, `reg.exe!QueryRegistry`, `kernelbase.dll!RegGetValueW`, `kernelbase.dll!RegQueryValueExW`, `kernelbase.dll!BaseRegQueryValueInternal`, `ntdll.dll!NtQueryValueKey`, and kernel-side `ntoskrnl.exe!NtQueryValueKey`, `EtwpTraceRegistry`, `EtwpTraceStackWalk`, and `KiSystemServiceStart`. The next proof step is now narrower: symbol-resolve or document that unlabeled init walker, or extend the explicit query lane into a natural boot/init or policy-replay consumer path.
